entries.description: use Suffix/Prefix/Middle pattern for infill (instead of Prefix/Suffix/Middle) as some models prefer this. (default: disabled)
entries.notes: Accepted on both server binaries through the shared `mlxcel::cli::infill_args::InfillArgs` group and honored by POST /infill: the flag moves the suffix block ahead of the prefix block while the middle marker stays last, which is upstream's swap exactly. b10621 declares it value-less with no environment binding, so this definition has none either. `infill_route_tests.rs::spm_infill_changes_the_prompt_the_server_actually_sends` asserts the flag reaches the served prompt rather than only the config.

Renders a chat-completions body through the loaded chat template and answers {"prompt": "..."} without generating. The render is the same `prepare_chat_request_with_cache` call /v1/chat/completions makes, so messages, tools, reasoning options and chat_template_kwargs are honored and what comes back is the prompt that request would have been served with. The MAX_TOOLS guard runs first, as it does on the generating routes, so an oversized tool array cannot reach Jinja2 through a route that does not generate.

Answers {"input_tokens": N} for a chat-completions body. The count runs the same render and the same encode the generation path runs (encode(prompt, add_special=true)), so it is the number of tokens that request would really have been prefilled with rather than an estimate that can drift from it.

Route separation done: /completion and /completions both reach the native handler and answer the b10621 native object (index, content, tokens, id_slot, stop, model, tokens_predicted, tokens_evaluated, generation_settings, prompt, has_new_line, truncated, stop_type, stopping_word, tokens_cached, timings with cache_n), and the streaming form ends with that same object rather than a [DONE] sentinel. The key set and order were taken from a capture of the pinned binary. #1466 closed the stop-sequence half: `stop` now truncates the emitted text, and stop_type reports "word" with the matched string in stopping_word, matching the pinned binary on the same request. #1441 then added `response_fields` projection, the `stream_options` block, the whole `n_predict` value domain including `-1` and the verified `0` prompt-only case, and the real prefill figures on every streaming frame, and corrected two `timings` derivations against the binary. The remaining differences are listed in divergence; two of them are #1441's and one belongs to #1440, which is why this entry stays deferred and stays filed under #1441.
divergence: `generation_settings` echoes the settings mlxcel actually resolved rather than b10621's full task_params block, so keys mlxcel has no analogue for are absent (#1441).

`tokens_cached` reports the prompt tokens mlxcel's KV prefix cache supplied for this request, while b10621 reports the slot's cache occupancy after it, which is `tokens_evaluated + tokens_predicted - 1`: a 51-token prompt answered with 4 tokens measured `tokens_cached: 54` on the pinned binary against mlxcel's cache-supplied count (#1441).
`return_tokens`, `return_progress`, `verbose`, `n_indent`, `t_max_predict_ms` and `n_cmpl` above 1 are refused with a diagnostic rather than honored (#1441).

entries.notes: Special tokens are rendered rather than skipped, as upstream's `tokens_to_str` does, and an absent or empty `tokens` answers {"content": ""} rather than failing. Bytes that cannot form a character come back as U+FFFD, which is what upstream emits too because its JSON writer runs with the replacing error handler.

Start it with `--embeddings`" because that flag really is accepted here.

Mounted and serving. The capability gate runs first and refuses a model whose vocabulary has no prefix, suffix and middle token with upstream's own wording, over the same spelling list llama-vocab.cpp scans; `input_prefix` and `input_suffix` are required, `input_extra` is validated as an array of {filename, text}, and the assembled prompt follows format_infill's ordering in both the default and --spm-infill forms. Two observable differences remain, recorded below, and they are why this entry is still deferred rather than supported.
divergence: Text in input_prefix, input_suffix, input_extra[].text, input_extra[].filename or prompt that contains one of the model's own FIM marker spellings is refused with a diagnostic; b10621 tokenizes those fields with parse_special off and serves the marker as literal text. mlxcel's generation entry takes a prompt string that is re-tokenized with parsing on, so the marker would otherwise silently restructure the prompt.

The FIM context is not truncated to the prefill batch: b10621 keeps only the last 3*(n_batch/4) prefix tokens and the first (n_batch/4) - (2 + prompt) suffix tokens, while mlxcel serves the whole prefix and suffix, consistent with its policy of clamping an over-long request rather than dropping prompt text.

entries.notes: All four aliases mounted (#1430); #1452 aligned the envelope. The Jina response now carries b10621's top-level "object": "list", and a request that spells its document list `texts` gets b10621's TEI shape instead: a bare array of {index, score} with `text` echoed under `return_text`. The Cohere `documents` / `return_documents` / `document` spelling mlxcel already served keeps working, and a body carrying both list spellings stays on the Jina envelope. The three shape errors use upstream's own wording. The route is served exactly when the operator asked for reranking; mlxcel spells that request as `--reranking`, `--pooling rank`, `--reranker-model <path>`, or a reranker checkpoint in -m, and the 501 body opens with upstream's "This server does not support reranking. Start it with `--reranking`".
The /reranking spelling of POST /rerank; all four paths reach one handler. See POST /rerank.

Answers {"input_tokens": N} for a Responses body. The body is flattened to the chat shape by the same translator /v1/responses uses, including previous_response_id and conversation rehydration, so the count covers the whole conversation the generation call would have prefilled rather than only the new turn.

All four b10621 switches are honored: `content` accepts the mixed shape (a string, or an array whose elements are strings or already-tokenized ids) and may be absent, in which case the answer is an empty token list rather than an error; `add_special` defaults to false; `parse_special` defaults to true and, when false, stops a special-token spelling written into the text from being recognized as that token; `with_pieces` switches the response to {id, piece} objects whose `piece` is a JSON string for valid UTF-8 and an array of byte values otherwise, so a token carrying part of a multi-byte character reassembles exactly.

entries.description: Number of completions to generate. If the input has multiple prompts, total outputs will be N prompts times n_cmpl
entries.notes: No equivalent: mlxcel serves exactly one completion per request, so there is no path that could return b10621's array of results. `n_cmpl` (and its `n` alias) is accepted at 1, the inert value, and any higher value is refused with a 400 naming the field and telling the caller to send one request per completion.

entries.description: Specify the minimum line indentation for the generated text in number of whitespace characters. Useful for code completion tasks
entries.notes: No equivalent: mlxcel has no minimum-indentation stop rule for fill-in-the-middle completions. Accepted at 0, the inert value, and refused with a 400 naming the field otherwise.

entries.description: Set the maximum number of tokens to predict. When 0, no tokens will be generated but the prompt is evaluated into the cache
entries.notes: Accepted through the b10621 spelling and its `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` aliases, over upstream's whole value domain rather than serde's. The `n_predict: 0` prompt-only case is now verified rather than assumed: the pinned binary emits exactly ONE token for it (not zero, despite the schema description), evaluates the whole prompt and reports `stop_type: "limit"`, and mlxcel answers the same one token on the same prompt against a real checkpoint. `-1`, upstream's spelling of "as many as the context allows", is accepted and clamped to the effective context window instead of being refused with a 422 as it was before. A value outside `[-1, INT32_MAX]` is refused with upstream's own wording, `Field 'n_predict': Value must be between -1 <= value <= 2147483647, but got -2`. An in-domain value is still silently clamped to the effective per-slot context window, which is what upstream does too.

entries.description: A list of response fields to return. Missing fields are omitted without error. Fields with a slash are unnested (e.g. generation_settings/n_predict moves n_predict to the root)
entries.notes: Implemented against the pinned binary rather than against the schema's own description, which is wrong about what the binary does. Upstream walks each path through the finished response splitting on `/` and stores the value under the WHOLE path string, so `generation_settings/n_predict` comes back as a root key literally named "generation_settings/n_predict"; it does not move `n_predict` to the root the way the description claims. Captured and reproduced: a missing path is omitted without an error, a path that walks into a non-object is omitted, `[""]` selects nothing, a repeated path yields one key, a nested object can be selected whole, the result keeps the order the request listed, and an empty list or a value that is not an array of strings (`"content"`, `["content", 5]`, `null`) returns the whole object with a 200 rather than a type error. Applied to the non-streaming body and to the final streaming frame only, which is also where upstream applies it: the per-token frames are unprojected on both sides.

entries.description: Include prompt processing progress events in stream mode
entries.notes: No equivalent: the mlxcel scheduler emits no prompt-processing progress events on this path, so there is nothing to attach to a stream frame. Accepted at false, the inert value, and refused with a 400 naming the field otherwise.

entries.description: Return the raw generated token ids in the `tokens` field
entries.notes: No equivalent on this path: mlxcel's streaming decoder emits detokenized text and does not surface the raw token ids to the native route. Accepted at false, the inert value, and refused with a 400 naming the field and pointing at POST /tokenize otherwise.

entries.description: Allows receiving each predicted token in real-time instead of waiting for the completion to finish
Whether to include usage information in the stream
entries.notes: Declared and type-checked instead of being dropped as an unknown key. Measured on the pinned binary serving a real checkpoint: on the native `/completion` route the block is inert, because the native final frame already carries `tokens_predicted`, `tokens_evaluated` and the whole `timings` object whether or not it is sent, so a request with `{"include_usage": true}` and one without it answer byte-identical bodies. A non-object value (`"stream_options": "garbage"`) is tolerated and ignored on both sides. mlxcel's OpenAI routes honor the same block the way b10621's do, emitting the trailing usage chunk with empty `choices`; that half predates this epic.

The subfield of the block above, modeled by the nested `NativeStreamOptions` struct so its type is validated rather than the value being read past. A present non-boolean is refused with upstream's own wording, `Field 'include_usage': type must be boolean, but is string`, measured against the pinned binary; absent or `null` resolves to the upstream default of false. The value has no observable effect on `/completion` in either implementation.

entries.description: Set a time limit in milliseconds for the prediction phase. The timeout triggers if generation exceeds this time (measured since the first token) and a newline has been generated. Useful for FIM applications
entries.notes: No per-request equivalent: mlxcel bounds a stalled decode with the server-wide --decode-timeout / MLXCEL_DECODE_TIMEOUT watchdog, which cannot be narrowed per request. Accepted at -1 or 0, the inert values, and refused with a 400 naming the field and the alternative otherwise.

entries.description: Include prompt processing and text generation speed information in each response
entries.notes: Accepted and honored: a streaming frame carries the timing block when it is set and omits it otherwise. The per-frame block now reports the real prefill figures rather than zeros. A one-shot prefill snapshot (`GenerateEvent::Prefill`, emitted by the scheduler when the first token is stamped) reaches the streaming route before the first frame, so `cache_n`, `prompt_n`, `prompt_ms` and `tokens_evaluated` carry the same values on every frame that the final frame reports, which is what the pinned binary does. Two derivations inside the block were also corrected against the binary in the same change: `prompt_n` is `tokens_evaluated - cache_n` (a fully cached prefix reports `prompt_n: 1` against `tokens_evaluated: 8` with `cache_n: 7`), and the generation rates divide by `predicted_n - 1` because `predicted_ms` starts at the first token, so `predicted_n: 4` with `predicted_ms: 15.132` reports `predicted_per_token_ms: 5.044`.

entries.description: Include __verbose field in the response with additional debug information
entries.notes: No equivalent: mlxcel has no __verbose debug block. Accepted at false, the inert value, and refused with a 400 naming the field and pointing at GET /slots and GET /metrics otherwise.
